chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hunting of falcons, hawks, dogs, and leopards, so he said: 'Do not eat the game of any of these except what you slaughtered (dhabaha), except the dog.'

I said: 'If it killed it?' He said: 'Eat it, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: "And what you have learned of the hunting beasts..." ... "So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of Allah over it."'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game caught by birds of prey versus dogs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between birds of prey and big cats, which require ritual slaughter (dhabaha) to be permissible, and trained hunting dogs, whose catch is eaten directly upon mentioning Allah's name. This ruling is grounded in Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:4, highlighting the Shia jurisprudential principle that the method of permissibility depends on the specific nature of the hunting animal and its training.
